acceptance_signals: The shared detector does not classify an sk- character sequence embedded inside a longer ordinary alphanumeric word, including the preserved task-view review identifier, as a secret token.
A real sk- token of the existing minimum length remains rejected at the start of text and after ordinary separators used in paths, assignments, quoted values, and messages.

Existing detection of GitHub-style tokens, AWS access keys, bearer tokens, JWT-like values, private-key headers, credential assignments, absolute Windows paths, and absolute POSIX paths remains unchanged.
Govern start can append a task.started event for a safe admitted task identifier containing task-view without weakening event schema, path, actor, authority, or privacy validation.
Scope observation can persist and reload a complete report containing a safe repository-relative path with task-view while an exact real secret-shaped value still fails closed.

Focused event-store, scope-observation, and development-session tests pass, followed by the complete Python 3.11 suite, task and repository governance checks, task JSON parsing, and git diff validation.

The dated log and STATUS.md record the observed review blocker, the exact bounded repair, validation evidence, residual security limits, and that the uncoached comprehension review remains a separate paused task to resume afterward.

No preserved proposal or review record is deleted, renamed, hidden, staged, or treated as repaired evidence; no Git operation, publication, release, deployment, dependency change, or external mutation occurs.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-a707d9a11cc14c089ed40c802d103ecf and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Make the shared local-record sensitive-token detector boundary-aware for the sk- token form so ordinary repository-relative identifiers containing an embedded word-suffix sequence can be persisted, while preserving rejection of real secret tokens, credential assignments, absolute paths, and all other existing sensitive patterns.

items: Changing secret-token matching can create a false negative, so the repair must add an explicit left lexical boundary only to the sk- branch and retain true-positive tests at start-of-text and after realistic separators.
The shared detector protects both event and evidence persistence, so focused tests must cover both direct local records and higher-level session and scope-observation paths.
A narrow matcher repair must not weaken credential-assignment, absolute-path, or other token-pattern checks.
The current worktree contains two untracked admitted review-task records and local AgentGov and Codex state that are outside this repair and must remain untouched.
The active uncoached review task is paused by this blocker; completing the repair does not itself complete, validate, or authorize the participant review.
Reviewed assumption: A secret token in supported local records begins at the start of text or after a non-word separator rather than in the middle of an ordinary alphanumeric word.
Reviewed assumption: The existing sk- minimum-length and allowed-character contract remains unchanged.
Reviewed assumption: The current event-store matcher is the single shared enforcement point for the two observed failures.
Reviewed unknown: Whether other benign identifiers contain equivalent embedded token-prefix collisions is unknown until broader validation runs.
Reviewed unknown: Whether any external consumer relies on rejecting sk- text embedded inside a longer ordinary word is unknown.
Reviewed unknown: The participant review outcome remains unknown and outside this repair.

title: Repair embedded sensitive-token prefix false positives
